title: Modules and Packages
text: These questions check that you can split code into modules, read the two module systems, use package.json and npm, and judge packages.

tasks.text: report.js contains import { totalKilograms } from "./garden.js" and Node says: Cannot use import statement outside a module. What's the fix?

const { crop, bed } = { crop: "Kale", bed: "B4", kg: 2.2 }
What is bed?
A classmate zips up their project, including a node_modules folder with 4,000 files. What should they send instead?
choices: The project without node_modules; package.json and package-lock.json let anyone recreate it with npm install

tasks.text: An assistant's example ends with a comment: // prints Saturday, June 12. Why should you run it rather than trust the comment?
tasks.answer: A comment showing output is a claim; the assistant may write what it expects rather than what the code does (e.g. the weekday was wrong for the year used). Running the code shows the real result.

tasks.text: List four things to check before installing an npm package, and one question to ask before looking for a package at all.
tasks.answer: Any four: weekly downloads/popularity; recent maintenance; who maintains it; number of dependencies; exact name (typosquatting); README/documentation; npm audit. First ask whether JavaScript or Node already has a built-in feature that does the job (or whether a few lines of your own would do).

tasks.text: Write a function summarize(harvest) that takes an object with crop, bed and kg properties, uses destructuring to get them, and returns a string like Kale from B4: 2.2 kg. Then write testSummarize, which logs summarize({ crop: "Kale", bed: "B4", kg: 2.2 }).

Create a project folder with package.json (type module), garden.js exporting two functions, and report.js importing them. Start a new chat with your updated learner profile and ask for a way to print a harvest report as a neatly aligned table in the terminal. (1) Paste the reply. (2) Did it use import, not require? Did it suggest a package, and if so, did it say how widely used it is? (3) Check any package on npmjs.com, and decide whether to install it or use a built-in (console.table exists). Explain your decision.
tasks.answer: Full credit: checks module style; notes package suggestion and popularity; a reasoned decision (console.table is built in). Replies vary, so grade the reasoning.
